harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Node1 now serves a CentOS 5-compatible local yum repository over HTTP. `sysstat-7.0.2-13.el5` was installed exclusively from it while the usual Vault repositories were unreachable. CentOS 5.11 and kernel 2.6.18-398.el5 were retained, and the repository recovered after reboot.
actions_performed: Enabled persistent HTTP serving through the native CentOS 5 httpd service.
Configured local-centos5 as the only enabled yum repository and disabled the unreachable Vault repositories.
Installed and verified sysstat from local-centos5.
Restarted node1 once and verified its boot identity changed and all required state recovered.

evidence.requirement: Serve a package repository from local storage
evidence.summary: Shows signed RPM content, generated repository metadata, HTTP service/listener, HTTP 200 response, and yum listing local-centos5 as enabled with one package.

evidence.requirement: Install a package from the local repository while usual remotes are unreachable
evidence.summary: Vault metadata access fails with TLS exit 35; yum installs sysstat with local-centos5 as the sole enabled transaction source.

evidence.requirement: Retain the installed OS release and kernel and use legacy-compatible software
evidence.summary: CentOS 5.11 and kernel 2.6.18-398.el5 remain unchanged; sysstat 7.0.2 and native httpd/createrepo packages are CentOS 5 builds.

Healthy baseline used boot ID bb84bb35-b74e-4546-8000-000000000000; reboot acknowledgement returned; post-restart boot ID changed to 84d2bcae-3fc7-4bed-8000-000000000000; httpd, HTTP repository data, RPM checksums, sysstat integrity, and the original kernel all recovered.
